Wait for the raster interrupt to clear the pending buffer switch at $08BB and for four increments of $0904. Then run the next pass and check the function keys.

Take the continuation off the stack so the race update can leave through a different path. Update speed and HUD, paint the road and lights, choose and place the truck tiles and advance the other race objects.
If the sprite list has room, choose an effect sequence for idle or steering left or right. Advance the selected pointer and place the sprite near the truck.
Choose a sequence based on the countdown state and step its color triples into the three start-light displays. $6E triggers an effect and $FF ends the sequence.
Start gantry active flag. The interrupt and render loop use it to stage extra flags and gantry cells.
Pending contact-animation state, including its initialized marker and countdown.

Update counter whose low bit is used when coasting.

High byte of the saved race continuation.
One lateral input step for each speed band. The driving loop adds it for right and subtracts it for left.
Extra signed lateral displacement per speed band. The driving loop chooses its sign from the curve direction.
Put the saved race continuation on the stack and return through it.
Reset the sprite staging lists, scan the controls, update the timed message and test the stage timeout before returning to the selected race state.
Handle recovery and collision checks first. Accelerate or brake for up/down, combine steering and the road bend, apply signed displacement, and render the result.
Ordered cutoffs for converting internal speed to a smaller speed-band index used by acceleration and steering.
Reduce speed if the truck at high speed is outside the road bounds, derive the engine sound pitch setting, then select the speed band.
Render while the start-light countdown is active with both clocks held. Once it ends, start the engine tone and wait for Up before entering the driving loop.
For recovery state $0B, center the truck and brake it to rest. Redraw the gantry, show the restart message and wait for a joystick input before restarting the light sequence.
Speed increment for each band used when Up is held.
Add the increment for the current speed band. Commit to $08E1 when the sum is below $7E.
Speed decrement for each band used when Down is held.
Subtract the current band's braking step from $08E1 and saturate to zero on underflow.
Apply a left displacement across the camera and truck fields. Clamp the earlier field at its end and pass the remainder to the other coordinate.
Apply a right displacement, trading the remainder between camera and truck when either crosses its threshold.
When the stage digits reach zero, enter the timeout sequence. Decelerate the truck and return to the rally setup once the timeout counter reaches $14.
Compare the rival's projected X and Y against the player. Walk roadside object records and use shape width, player X and the speed-dependent depth threshold to recognize contact.
Dispatch only while a contact animation is pending. Object classes $3D and $44 use the cone path, and other classes use the moving tile cells.
Choose the cone-contact placement or load the four transient animation graphics starting at shape $34.
Select the next shape index for the current staged animation and write its character indices in a three-by-three block.
Gate the spawn by speed, timer and route settings. Choose a speed, lateral lane offset and color, then project the rival from relative speed and road edges.
Interpret the collision or obstacle reaction script. Commands can steer the truck, adjust speed, trigger an effect, select a truck drawing pose, or finish the sequence.
Select the writing sprite-buffer index, clear its sprite control masks and start the bit accumulator for the next sprite.
Look up a composite in the pointer table at $180B. Read its width and height and place each nonnegative sprite pointer at 24 physical pixels per column, accumulating the X high bits.
Two NOP opcodes following the sprite-composite routine's return.

Left edge for each projected road row, used by vehicle projection and speed limiting.

Work table filled by the perspective setup and adjusted during the scenery-height phase.

Order the two edge contribution pointers by side, then combine their entries at the row indices supplied by $24D1. The branch at $26D1 is modified for the fork overlay.
Mutable branch displacement. The fork state changes the row dispatch path through $26CA.
Accumulate distance from the speed band's 16-bit step. When it reaches the first byte of the route command times ten, subtract the distance and dispatch by the command class.
Decode the high three bits of the route opcode, or dispatch the small opcodes directly. Route commands install scenery, direction, obstacle streams, branches, colors, stage timing and notices.
At the branch terminator, the truck's lateral coordinate $08E3 selects the stream pointer and sign list. The threshold is $50.
Decode eight bytes holding the fork opcode, two stream pointer words and two sign-group indices. Set the fork overlay and arm it for the later $40 command.
Resolve an obstacle formation by the little-endian pointers at $EEB9. Reset the formation offset and align its initial distance with the frame's progress.
Inspect the full route opcode below $20. Opcode 8 takes the four display digits of a new stage timer from the stream.

Recover the six-character city offset and print the left branch name.
Inline HUD cursor for the right destination.
Print the six-character right branch label and advance past the road command.
For opcode 4, set the active route pointer and restart pointer to the supplied low and high bytes and calculate the new distance threshold.
Add the command's byte length to the route pointer. If the next distance byte is $FF, restore the last stream restart address.
Update character graphics, obstacle scheduling and route state. Redraw the road and scenery pieces and lay down active roadside objects for this pass.
Multiply the route record's first byte by ten with shifts and additions, leaving the 16-bit threshold in $6C/$6D.
Draw a five-by-four array of consecutive character indices into both screen buffers and color RAM. X selects the marker and Y the placement column.
For a pending $C0 route event, generate destination glyph numbers and copy successive distance variants of the chosen shape into both character sets.
Advance through the chosen obstacle formation as distance accumulates, inserting depth, mapped shape, and lateral placement into the active road-object array.
Compute the sign step from speed, fork side and the current direction-sign state.
Move the current left road overlay table pointer by the distance step until its negative end marker.
Move the right overlay pointer while its activation flag is set. At the negative terminator, restore the default curve table and clear the sign step.
Advance or rewind the scenery-height phase and use it to adjust the visible road's depth. Shift the $23C9 row indices into the working row table.
Look up a rectangular shape and assign it a destination character index. Copy each glyph into both race character sets beginning at $7800 and $F800.
Install the light graphics and gantry pieces in the character banks. Also install the finish banner when the finish state is active.
Write the selected gantry uprights and banner characters into both screen buffers and their attributes into color RAM.
Compute fixed-point increments from the near and far offsets and fill a row table through $06. Patch the loop direction when endpoint order reverses.
Mutable INY or DEY opcode. The first interpolation routine changes it with the endpoint ordering.
Compute fixed-point increments for the other road edge and fill its row table through $06.
Mutable row-index increment opcode used by the second interpolation path.
Clear selected rows and strips in the inactive screen chosen by $0E.
Select the output rows for the inactive buffer. Look up shape 1 and combine the computed edge positions with the road-wedge glyphs.
Operand patched from the left road-edge glyph for this row.
Operand patched from the right road-edge glyph for this row.
Choose the current screen buffer, step each active depth by the current speed band, and project the roadside tile patterns relative to the road edge offset tables.
Clear pending route and obstacle state, select the default edge tables and derive the first distance threshold.
Write the decimal display of A to the HUD by dividing into digit positions.

Set the speed field's display color and pass current speed to the decimal renderer.

Set the displayed speed cache to $FF so $3727 will redraw the field.
Use X as the index in the four-word message pointer table and pass its address to the HUD message reader.
Set the message index and duration, reset the eight-update divider and display the selected message.
Count the eight-update divider and decrement the duration on its expiry. Refresh the message while the remaining duration is nonzero.
Write descending tile numbers to a strip in both race matrices.
Fetch bytes through $06/$07, advancing the pointer. Pass each byte to the character writer until a caret, then return with the pointer at the following byte.
Pull the return address and read a caret-terminated byte stream after the call. Jump to the byte following its terminator.
Dispatch through $F200. In normal mode, convert the character to a glyph index and write both screen buffers and color RAM. Control bytes reposition the cursor or select the attribute.
Read the current controls and return the fire bit isolated in A.
Read three-byte shape, column and row commands after the call until $FF. Write their consecutive character indices and color bytes into the two work planes.
Read three-byte shape, column and row commands after the call until $FF. Copy each shape's glyph rows and write its color attributes into the bitmap planes.

Initialize the high-score matrix with consecutive cell indices.
Copy $140 bytes from the $6000 font into the character bank used by the leaderboard.
